To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

overexpression of superoxide dismutase, an enzyme that catalyzes the dismutation of superoxide anion to hydrogen peroxide, in rat sympathetic neurons, using an expression system based on adenovirus, substantially protected the neurons from the effects of withdrawal of nerve growth factors.
overexpression of copper/zinc-superoide dismutase, an enzyme that scavenges superoxide radicals, inhibits the death caused by NGF withdrawal in rat sympathetic neurons.

overexpression of the antioxidant copper/zinc-superoxyde dismutase (SOD) in sympathetic neurons protects the cells from programmed cell death induced by NGF withdrawal, that treatment of the neurons with the cytokine TGF beta1 delays cell death caused by NGF withdrawal and that the protective effect of TGF beta1 is blocked by the antioxidant SOD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of reactive oxygen species in the regulation of programmed cell death of neurons in the central nervous system.
the role of reactive oxygen species in neuronal cell death and the potential use of antioxidants as neuroprotectants.
the role of reactive oxygen species in the death of sympathetic neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
overexpression of SOD1 protects rat superior cervical ganglion cells against programmed cell death by preventing the generation of reactive oxygen species.
the expression of human Cu/Zn-SOD inhibits the death caused by NGF withdrawal in rat sympathetic neurons.
the expression of the enzyme superoxide dismutase protects the neurons from death, and this is consistent with the idea that reactive oxygen species play a role in the death of these neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
overexpression of Cu/Zn-SOD protects rat sympathetic neurons from death by NGF withdrawal and that this protection may be mediated by a decrease in reactive oxygen species.
reactive oxygen species play an important role in the programmed cell death of neurons.

overexpression of superoxide dismutase inhibiting the death of rat superior cervical ganglion (SCG) neurons caused by withdrawal nerve growth factor ( NGF) and treatment with the cytokine, transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-beta) 1, delayed cell death caused by NGF withdrawal in rat SCG neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of a superoxide dismutase gene in rat superior cervical ganglion neuron cell cultures can protect the cells from programmed cell death, which is induced by NGF withdrawal, suggesting a role for oxidative stress in the death process.
the expression of the enzyme Cu,ZnSOD in neurons protects them against programmed cell death caused by the withdrawal of nerve growth factors.
the expression of human Cu/Zn-superoxide dismtase in rat superior cervical ganglion cells protects the cells from the cell death that occurs when NGF is withdrawn from the culture medium.
